notes.summary: All six whole qualified grants, their bound annotations, and essential original units were read. S291 acceptance retains native218 source/combined FAIL and historical INCONCLUSIVE.
notes.detailedSummary: All 28 mathematical packet files and four primary files have verified bound hashes. Whole-packet reading coverage includes every annotation and the three unreviewed working files. Primary unit numbering uses literal LF. Whole BBGS3.15 ends at LF670. Original rational coefficient/weight definitions, actual real extensions, primitive lattice normals, Euclidean unit normals, and product signs remain distinct. Historical saved expansions are not treated as actual nativeFINAL records.
notes.text:
The supplied mathematical inputs were read as data. Exactly six whole grants were retained: A224, B225, R230, S262, S272 and S291, including every bound clarification, acceptance, source-correction, reader, ledger and scope record. Working296, working297 and working299 were read entirely and independently reconstructed; they were not seventh grants. This note registers the qualified supplied facts used by subsequent notes. It does not independently re-prove every previously granted operator or classification result.

A224 retains its finite actual-PA strict-growth obstruction and active-coefficient qualifications. B225 retains saturated-covolume stationary flux, positive spanning, and its finite-global noncompactness scope. R230 retains dominating continuous completion and continuity of the actual unrestricted all-C_b envelope, without claiming that raw printed-PC functions are automatically continuous. S262 retains its finite-PA obstruction/contact sector, rational-reference constructions, genuine completed-domain operator conclusions, and graph sector. S272 retains actual-reference real coefficient decompositions, signed/zero intermediate weights, completed-domain requirements, dimension-zero qualifications, and the distinctions between global-vague uniformity, ordinary weak-net continuity and fixed-C weak/BL uniformity. S291 retains its compact balanced-atlas sector, full-affine primal approximation, independent-bouquet sector and literal noncompact obstruction, with all source and history qualifications. These sector results do not classify arbitrary positive-dimensional overlaps.

The four frozen originals are the sole primary sources. BMPS is arXiv v1, https://arxiv.org/pdf/2603.08664v1, submitted 9 March 2026, manuscript dated 10 March 2026. PDF SHA-256: 5cf7e68ee9113f1dc813f9aefa5f9ca72cba02fc4fa688f1a61e4b7f0d1223e7. Text SHA-256: c4475ad5cf4e8fce3eb6add155fdb81e352cbe079ca0d7646553f8a3e8ad9271. Essential whole immediate units were read in literal-LF ranges 254–301, 418–508, 509–614, 689–847, 886–894, 1005–1034, 1741–1747 and 2253–2358. Delegated external arguments, the raw-PC automatic-continuity assertion and the printed all-PC density equivalence were not imported.

BBGS is the publisher version at https://link.springer.com/content/pdf/10.1007/s00209-021-02869-6.pdf, Math. Z. 301 (2022), 1631–1674, published 24 January 2022. PDF SHA-256: c2817a01e51ac3781e94005cb587c185ac7e6cc5fe654feda6c5341eaf6a5846. Text SHA-256: 87f8f8d2d51e523c4ecf5f8429875da16994abbe74132ce05886d1782e90b635. Whole immediate units were read in literal-LF ranges 196–242, 379–413, 443–533, 533–598, 604–670 and 675–704. In particular, whole commutation Proposition3.15 includes its final equation and proof ending at LF670; LF667 is insufficient.

BMPS's printed PCC has rational endpoints, real nonnegative coefficients and a possibly real barycenter; the common face may equal an assigned cell. Its original lattice coefficient and weight definitions are rational. BBGS supplies a separate actual-real-weight Euclidean model with inward unit conormals and negative product sign. The fresh proofs explicitly bridge primitive and unit normals by saturated covolumes instead of relabeling the original definitions.

S291 mathematical acceptance coexists with native218 original-source FAIL, combined FAIL and retrospective-history INCONCLUSIVE. Both correction and reader records remain binding. The bound history distinguishes seven actual native218 FINAL notes from seven later expanded saved notes, and the earlier author216 actual six-note FINAL from its saved terminal-newline variant. No unbound historical file was opened and no past runtime event is certified here. Corrected source reading does not retroactively convert those reports to PASS.

Records are in source-application-ledger.md, reports/input-audit.json, logs/read-ranges.jsonl and logs/initial-observations.md. Rerun metadata verification with python code/audit_inputs.py. notes.summary: All six working299 units have independent proofs: uniform closed-cell Lipschitz bounds and bounded ambient supports on entire incident cells under strictly positive actual real balancing.
notes.detailedSummary: The proof reconstructs real-endpoint PCC by rational perspective density; active-normal distance estimates and all-slack insets; saturated-covolume flux and positive spanning; finite incident derivatives and a sublinear support envelope; and induction over every finite face, including lineality and minimal positive-dimensional faces. Bounds have the form A_X C+B_X G. Gamma need not be PC or positive-growth. The conclusion concerns cells and intrinsic polygonal paths, not arbitrary ambient distances across nonincident cells.
notes.text:
Fix a finite pure-dimensional globally embedded rational polyhedral complex, retaining all closed faces and balancing at every codimension-one face. Top weights are strictly positive actual real numbers. Fix a rational refinement carrying the actual continuous real PA gamma, affine on each cell, with intrinsic gradient norms at most G. Suppose f is continuous printed-PC and |f-gamma|≤C, C≥0. The empty complex is vacuous. The following argument proves geometry-dependent uniform bounds for every closed cell and for supports at every minimal-face point.

L0, real PCC and inherited-cell convexity. For a real feasible configuration with assigned cells sigma_i containing tau, delete zero coefficients and write t_i=alpha_i x_i. Conditions alpha_i≥0, sum alpha_i=1, x_i∈sigma_i and sum t_i∈tau become rational weak linear inequalities/equalities: A_i t_i≤alpha_i b_i, together with affine-hull equations. At the given configuration impose every active row as an equality. This minimal feasible face has a rational particular solution and rational kernel basis by Gaussian elimination. Rational combinations approximate the given point while preserving all inactive strict slacks and positive alpha_i. Thus rational feasible configurations approximate it; endpoints t_i/alpha_i and centers sum t_i are rational. Apply the permitted rational-center PCC subfamily and use continuity. Relative-interior centers remain relative-interior; a boundary center uses its minimal inherited face. This proves PCC with real endpoints, centers and coefficients. For any two points of one inherited closed cell, their barycenter lies in a minimal face contained in that cell; assigning both endpoints to the same cell proves convexity. No faces are coarsened and no raw-PC continuity is assumed.

Finite-cone foundations. A nonnegative column representation can be reduced to independent columns: choose a dependence b with a positive entry and subtract s b, where s=min(a_i/b_i) over b_i>0. Nonnegativity and the represented vector are preserved, and one positive coefficient disappears. Repetition ends at an independent sublist. Its inverse column map bounds the coefficient sum by K_I times the represented norm. A finite maximum over independent sublists gives a uniform K. This also proves cone closedness by subsequences with one sublist and bounded convergent coefficients. Nearest-point first variation separates an outside point w from a closed cone: if k is its projection, v=w-k has v·k=0, v·z≤0 on the cone and v·w>0.

For later polyhedral applications, rational finite generation is also elementary. Split off the rational joint-kernel lineality. In the pointed quotient the sum of oriented defining nonnegative rows is strictly positive off zero. Its unit-value section is bounded, since an unbounded sequence would normalize to a nonzero joint-kernel cone vector. A bounded polyhedron is the convex hull of its finitely many vertices: at a nonvertex move in both signs of an active-row kernel direction to additional active rows, then recurse on rank. Vertices solve finitely many independent systems and are rational for rational data. Add both signs of a lineality basis. Homogenization gives a polyhedron as a finite hull plus recession cone. Conversely, projection of such a finite representation is polyhedral by eliminating variables: pair every lower bound with every upper bound, retaining rows without that variable; absent one-sided bounds allow an unbounded interval. This elimination preserves rational spatial data.

L1, distance. Work in the relative affine hull so equalities are removed. For nonempty P={n_j·x≤b_j}, choose a nearest z and put w=x-z. If w is outside the cone of active outward normals, the preceding separation gives a direction v with n_j·v≤0 on active rows and w·v>0. Small positive steps from z respect inactive rows by their strict slack, contradicting nearest-point variation. Thus w=sum lambda_j n_j on active rows. Independent-column reduction gives sum lambda_j≤H||w|| with H depending only on the row list. With delta(x)=max(0,max_j(n_j·x-b_j)),
||w||²=sum lambda_j(n_j·x-b_j)≤H delta(x)||w||,
so dist(x,P)≤H delta(x). Zero rows are harmless; empty lists give distance zero; dimension zero is immediate.

For each face tau include every own facet row and every incident-top-cell row strictly slack on ri(tau). Other incident rows vanish identically on tau: a valid affine inequality vanishing at a relative-interior point cannot change sign locally. Choose a rational relative-interior point and a rational margin below every listed slack. Strengthen all listed rows by that margin. The inset is nonempty, and every y∈tau violates its strengthened rows by at most that margin. The distance bound therefore supplies an inset z with ||z-y||≤D_tau uniformly, including near lower faces and at infinity. Empty lists and point faces have D_tau=0. A fixed anchor alone would not prove this estimate. For finitely many assigned cone generators, choose one rational epsilon_tau>0 so z+epsilon_tau v_j belongs to its assigned top cell for every inset z: active rows respect cone directions, inactive rows have the strengthened slack, and affine-hull equations are preserved.

L2, actual-real positive spanning. At ri(tau), incident top-cell tangent cones are fixed rational cones containing T_tau as lineality. Choose finite rational generators including both signs of a tangent basis; let E_tau be their span. Stars inherit balance because their facets come from original facets containing tau with unchanged tangent lattices. Refinement preserves it: newly inserted interior facets have opposite primitive quotient vectors and equal inherited weights; subdivided old facets retain the original relation.

For a facet rho of sigma, saturation makes N_sigma/N_rho free of rank one. A facet lattice basis plus a primitive quotient lift is a cell lattice basis. Consequently the primitive lift's orthogonal projection has length c_sigma/c_rho, where c denotes Euclidean saturated covolume, and equals (c_sigma/c_rho) times the inward unit conormal. Actual balancing therefore becomes sum rho_sigma nu_sigma/rho=0 with positive Euclidean density rho_sigma=w_sigma c_sigma.

If the finite closed generator cone were a proper subset of E_tau, separation would give a nonzero linear lambda nonnegative on it and positive on some incident cone. Apply divergence to the constant projected gradient of lambda on each d-dimensional cone intersected with the unit ball, with density rho_sigma. Planar outward facet fluxes cancel by the displayed relation. Outer spherical flux is sum rho_sigma integral lambda(theta), nonnegative everywhere and strictly positive on a relatively open patch of a full-dimensional cone. This contradicts zero divergence. Dimension one uses the endpoint formula; whole lines have antipodal cancellation. Lineality is allowed. If T_tau=E_tau its two-sided basis already fills the span; dimension zero has E_tau={0}. Thus the conical hull is all E_tau. Independent-column bounds now represent both v and -v with nonnegative assigned-generator coefficients of sum at most K_tau||v||.

L3, directional costs. Assume f|tau has global Lipschitz constant M_tau; for a point this is zero. At y∈ri(tau), choose the inset z and xi=z-y, ||xi||≤D_tau. On an assigned incident cone define h_sigma(w)=lim as t decreases to zero of [f(y+t w)-f(y)]/t. Convex secants give a limit in [-infinity,infinity), with finite upper bound. Positive homogeneity holds. Midpoint convexity at y+2t u and y+2t v proves subadditivity within a cone even before finiteness: there is no +infinity term, and a minus-infinite right term forces a minus-infinite upper limit. Tangent derivatives agree across cells and |h(±xi)|≤M_tau D_tau.

Since z+epsilon v_j is in the assigned cell, bounded difference from the SAME affine gamma restriction gives h(xi+epsilon v_j)≤2C+G(D_tau+epsilon||v_j||). Subadditivity using epsilon v_j=(xi+epsilon v_j)+(-xi) yields
h(v_j)≤U_tau=[2C+(G+M_tau)D_tau]/epsilon_tau+G V_tau,
where V_tau=max||v_j||. Initially this permits -infinity.

Every finite zero-sum list of assigned feasible directions has feasible endpoints y+t w_a for one common small t. Real PCC with equal coefficients gives sum [f(y+t w_a)-f(y)]/t≥0. If any incident h(w) were -infinity, append a fixed-generator representation of -w from L2, scaling directions by their coefficients. Appended quotients have finite upper limits bounded by their coefficients times U_tau. The total would tend to -infinity, a contradiction. Hence every incident derivative is finite, and passage to the limit gives nonnegative cost for every zero-sum assigned list.

Let H_y(v) be the infimum of summed incident derivative costs over ALL finite assigned-direction decompositions summing to v. Fixed generators give H_y(v)≤K_tau U_tau||v||. Append their representation of -v to any decomposition to obtain the reverse bound -K_tau U_tau||v||≤H_y(v). The empty decomposition and zero-sum inequality give H_y(0)=0. Scaling decompositions proves positive homogeneity; concatenating approximate minimizers proves subadditivity. Thus H_y is finite sublinear and globally Lipschitz.

The elementary full-space epigraph-support argument gives a linear p_y≤H_y, of norm at most K_tau U_tau by testing both directions. Extend it by zero on E_tau's orthogonal complement. For every x in an entire incident cell, x-y is a feasible cone direction and convex secants give
f(x)-f(y)≥h_sigma(x-y)≥H_y(x-y)≥p_y·(x-y).
This is an entire-cell support, not a germ. Only E_tau={0} permits the trivial p_y=0 shortcut; a point face in positive dimension can require a nonzero ambient support bound.

The epigraph-support foundation used here and in the induction has a direct proof. On an interior cube a finite convex function is bounded above by vertex values and below by reflection about its center. Extending secants within a smaller cube gives local Lipschitzness, hence continuity. Project points just below the graph to the closed cube epigraph and take a unit-normal limit. Its vertical component is nonpositive and cannot vanish, since a nonzero horizontal functional cannot attain its maximum at the center of a spatial neighborhood. Divide by the negative vertical component to get a relative affine lower support. Convex secants extend it over the whole convex domain. This also proves the full-space double-conjugate identity from affine supports. Point domains have zero relative subgradient.

L4, all-face induction. Process every finite face by dimension. Earlier supports at proper-face points, using each point's minimal face, support the whole current tau because a top cell containing tau is incident to that minimal face. Let B be their maximum norm bound, or zero if none exist. At q∈ri(tau), take ANY relative subgradient a. For a≠0 follow e=a/||a||. If the ray reaches a finite proper-face endpoint z at time t0, the subgradient at q and earlier entire-cell support at z give t0||a||≤f(z)-f(q)≤t0 B. If the ray remains forever, bounded f-gamma makes its long secant tend exactly to the affine gamma slope, at most G; the subgradient bounds it below by ||a||. Therefore all relative subgradients have norm at most max(B,G). Two subgradients give Lipschitzness on ri(tau); mix boundary points with a fixed relative-interior point and use continuity to obtain GLOBAL Lipschitzness on the closed, possibly unbounded tau. Apply L3 next. Point faces use intrinsic M_tau=0 but retain their ambient L3 support bounds.

This starts even when minimal faces have positive dimension and no vertices: finite ray exits would produce proper faces, so the infinite-ray argument supplies the initial bound. Lineality is included. Each step uses finite geometric K,D,epsilon,V and produces a bound linear in C and G. Taking coefficient-wise maxima over finitely many earlier faces and finally over all faces gives finite A_X,B_X with both Lipschitz and support bounds at most A_X C+B_X G.

L5 is the resulting uniform closed-cell/path assertion and its scoped regularization input. Sum cellwise bounds along a polygonal path whose segments lie in cells. No ambient-distance bound across nonincident cells or components follows; parallel balanced lines with different affine slopes already prevent such a statement. Gamma's PC, growth, coefficient rationality and quotient-normal independence were unused in this proof.

Full arguments and coverage are retained in argument.md, P05.1-paper.tex and reports/proof-coverage.json. These are mathematical proofs offered as unverified drafts; finite execution does not establish their correctness. This theorem is not a complete original classification.

notes.summary: All five working296 units are reconstructed: exact whole-affine convex extensions and genuine rational-carrier real PA majorants for one Lipschitz cell.
notes.detailedSummary: An integer rational-violation penalty gives a proper auxiliary Gamma exactly equal to the actual affine reference on the entire cell. The norm-infimum extension is finite, convex, globally Lipschitz and exact; its Gamma-bounded maximum receives no MA. The full-affine primal construction uses actual possibly irrational dual slopes, continuous boundary fibers, rational spatial samples with actual heights, exact recession rays and rational projected lower faces. Finite contacts are exact before common dyadic shifts. No entire-face gluing is obtained.
notes.text:
Let sigma be a nonempty closed rational convex cell in its rational affine hull Q, with inherited Euclidean metric. Let ell(x)=a·x+b be actual real affine and satisfy a·v>0 for every nonzero v∈rec(sigma). Let f be finite continuous convex, |f-ell|≤C, and globally L-Lipschitz on sigma. For the balanced-complex application, n2 supplies L. The distance, finite-generation, projection and subgradient foundations below use the proved results of n2.

C1 is the relative nearest-point distance estimate proved in n2: for sigma={A_j·x≤b_j}, delta(x)=max(0,max_j(A_j·x-b_j)), dist(x,sigma)≤H delta(x). Affine-hull equalities are removed by working in Q. Empty lists and dimension zero are included.

C2. Define Gamma=ell+kappa delta, with positive integer kappa. It equals ell on ALL sigma. Delta has rational spatial walls; adding the same real ell to every piece preserves those walls. Put r(v)=max(0,max_j A_j·v). Gamma's recession is h(v)=a·v+kappa r(v). On the compact unit section of rec(sigma), a·v has a positive minimum if that section is nonempty. Positivity persists in a neighborhood; on its compact complement r has a positive minimum. A sufficiently large integer kappa makes h positive there too. If the recession unit section is empty, r is positive throughout the unit sphere. Hence h≥c||v|| for some c>0. Gamma-h is bounded by its finitely many affine constants, giving coercive proper growth. On a point Q, Gamma is simply ell and the recession condition is vacuous. Gamma is an AUXILIARY extension, not a replacement of actual gamma elsewhere on X.

C3. Choose rational M≥L and define fhat(x)=inf over y∈sigma of f(y)+M||x-y||. A fixed y0 gives a finite upper bound. Lipschitzness and the triangle inequality give the lower bound f(y0)-M||x-y0||. For x∈sigma every term is at least f(x), and y=x gives equality. Triangle inequalities give global M-Lipschitzness. Convexity follows by choosing approximate minimizers at two points, combining their y-values inside sigma, using convexity and the norm inequality, and letting the tolerance vanish. Infimum attainment is not required.

At a nearest y∈sigma,
fhat(x)≤ell(x)+C+(M+||a||)dist(x,sigma)≤Gamma(x)+C
when kappa is also at least H(M+||a||). Increasing kappa preserves C2. Set F=max(fhat,Gamma-C). Then F is finite continuous convex on all Q, Gamma-C≤F≤Gamma+C, and F=f on the entire sigma because Gamma=ell there and f≥ell-C. F need not be PA and receives no Monge–Ampere measure.

C4 reconstructs the full-affine mechanism. A finite convex real PA Gamma is the maximum of its actual affine pieces: each full-dimensional affine piece is a global support by convex secants. Thus Gamma=max_j(a_j·x+b_j), h=max_j a_j·v, and D=conv{a_j} is a compact possibly irrational polytope. Coercivity puts zero in its interior. If zero is outside, nearest-point variation gives h(v)<0; at a boundary point, normalized nearest-point normals from outside points tending to zero have a unit limit with h(v)≤0. Both contradict positive h. Both Gamma-h and F-h are bounded.

For the actual conjugate F*(p)=sup_x(p·x-F(x)), its finite domain is EXACTLY D. For p∈D, p·x≤h(x) gives a uniform finite upper bound and evaluation at zero a lower bound. If p∉D, let q be its nearest point and v=p-q. First variation gives h(v)≤v·q<v·p; along tv the conjugate tends to infinity. On D, F* is finite bounded convex lower semicontinuous, as a supremum of continuous affine functions.

Boundary continuity is essential and follows without rational dual facets. For a finite lower semicontinuous convex g on a compact polytope, vertex values bound g above by B. At p choose r below all inactive facet slacks divided by row norms. For nearby q in the polytope, z=p+r(q-p)/||q-p|| remains feasible: active rows do not increase and inactive rows have the chosen margin. Convexity gives g(q)≤g(p)+(||q-p||/r)(B-g(p)); lower semicontinuity supplies the opposite limit. Thus g is continuous at every boundary fiber. Use the relative hull in degenerate dimensions.

Continuity of F lets rational spatial samples compute the same supremum defining F*. At each p∈D choose a rational sample s within eta/2 of that supremum. Continuity on D makes its error less than eta in a neighborhood. Compactness gives finitely many rational samples A with F*-eta≤g_A≤F* on ALL D, where g_A(p)=max_s(p·s-F(s)). Append ANY prescribed finite rational contact set from sigma; inequalities are preserved. Heights are actual real F(s), equal to f(s) at those contacts, with no rounding.

The rational recession cones of Gamma's carrier cover Q: along any ray a subsequence lies in one cell, whose rows show that its direction is in that cell's recession cone. On each cone h is linear. Sign chambers of their defining homogeneous rational hyperplanes, together with rational coordinate hyperplanes, give a finite pointed rational refinement. With its rational generators r_k,
epi h=cone{(r_k,h(r_k)),(0,1)}.
Spatial rays are rational; heights are actual reals and the recession is exact.

Form E=conv{(s,F(s)):s∈A}+epi h. It is closed because a compact hull plus a closed cone is closed, and it is a finite real polyhedron by n2's elimination proof. Its projection is all Q: from any one sample add the cone point (x-s,h(x-s)). Every fiber contains an upward ray. Convex secants and bounded F-h give F(x+v)≤F(x)+h(v). Hence convex combinations of sample lifts followed by cone addition remain in epi F. Thus E⊂epi F; each nonempty vertical fiber is bounded below and has an attained finite bottom P(x). P is finite convex on all Q, hence continuous by the cube argument.

Optimization over the hull and cone gives P*=g_A on D and infinity outside D. The full-space affine-support/double-conjugate proof from n2 yields F≤P≤F+eta globally. At every retained sample, its exact lift lies in E, so P(s)≤F(s); the lower bound gives equality.

Rational spatial geometry requires a separate check. Full projection and upward closure rule out vertical facets; every graph face can be exposed with negative vertical coefficient. Such a face selects a subset of the lifted samples and a subset of zero-exposing-value recession rays; it excludes the vertical ray. Its projection is therefore a hull of rational locations plus a cone of rational spatial rays, a rational polyhedron. On a lower graph face, projection is an affine isomorphism, and unique graph heights ensure that projected intersections are common faces. These finitely many projected faces cover Q and give a genuine rational carrier despite irrational heights.

The scalar real PA condition also holds. Continuous affine coefficient tuples on this rational carrier satisfy homogeneous rational matching equations, tested on rational affine bases of shared faces. Gaussian elimination gives a rational solution basis; clearing denominators makes each basis function have integral lattice slopes and rational constants. The actual tuple for P is a finite real linear combination of those literal PA functions. No arbitrary maximum closure with irrational switching walls is used. Full-space convexity directly implies printed PCC by Jensen.

The recession of E is exactly epi h: cone inclusion is immediate, while division by a recession parameter removes the bounded hull part and leaves a limit in the closed cone. Thus P∞=h. Intersect its carrier with sigma and retain all faces. This gives a finite rational carrier, convex real PA restriction p, f≤p≤f+eta, exact prescribed rational contacts, and actual recession ell: r(v)=0 on rec(sigma), so h(v)=a·v. Bounded f-ell gives that same recession. No isolated-cell mixed operator is applied.

An exact real-height illustration is F(x)=sqrt(1+x²), Gamma=|x|. Samples at ±1 have height sqrt(2); their hull plus epi|v| gives P=sqrt(2)+max(0,|x|-1), with rational walls ±1 and exact contacts. For r=|x|≤1, P²-F²=1-r²; for r≥1 it equals 2(sqrt(2)-1)(r-1). Also P-(sqrt(2)-1) equals 1 or r, respectively, each at most F. Thus 0≤P-F≤sqrt(2)-1 on the entire real line. The program separately checks 67 specified rational inputs using exact Q(sqrt(2)) arithmetic.

C5. Choose eta_n=2^-n and unshifted p_n with 0≤p_n-f≤eta_n. Then g_n=p_n+4eta_n satisfies 4eta_n≤g_n-f≤5eta_n and g_n-g_(n+1)≥4eta_n-5eta_(n+1)=3eta_n/2>0. It decreases uniformly to f with unchanged recession. These dyadic shifts can be chosen commonly, but they do not create missing face compatibility. Exact f-contacts belong to the unshifted p_n. Point cells reduce to constants.

These proofs establish the five single-cell units and are retained in argument.md and P05.1-paper.tex. They do not establish entire shared-face equality or common ambient supports for independently chosen approximants on different cells.

notes.summary: Whole working297 is verified: the unbalanced orthant example has sharp uniform finite real-PA approximation floor 1/2.
notes.detailedSummary: The example is continuous convex, differs from x+y by a term in [0,1], and has the same positive cell recession. Every finite continuous PA function on the convex orthant is globally Lipschitz. The pairs (n²,0) and (n²,n^-2) force error at least 1/2, attained by gamma+1/2. Its unbalanced boundary star excludes it from working299 and shows that the single-cell Lipschitz premise cannot be dropped.
notes.text:
On sigma={(x,y):x,y≥0}, set gamma=x+y and f=gamma+b, b=max(0,1-sqrt(xy)). On the open quadrant the Hessian quadratic form of sqrt(xy) is -(y dx-x dy)²/[4(xy)^(3/2)], so it is concave. Continuity and inward approximation extend concavity to the closed orthant. Therefore 1-sqrt(xy), its maximum with zero, and f are continuous convex. Since 0≤b≤1, f has bounded affine difference and recession f∞(v)=v1+v2, strictly positive for every nonzero orthant recession direction. This proves B1.

Every continuous finite real PA function a on a convex cell is globally Lipschitz: a segment meets each of finitely many carrier cells in an interval, and their finitely many interval endpoints partition it into affine subsegments. Sum the gradient bounds across that partition, using continuity. This allows real coefficients and even real spatial walls. Thus a-gamma has some finite Lipschitz constant L.

Let z_n=(n²,0), w_n=(n²,n^-2). Their distance is n^-2, while b(z_n)=1 and b(w_n)=0. For finite e=||a-f||∞, triangle inequalities give 1≤2e+L n^-2. For each fixed finite PA a, let n tend to infinity to obtain e≥1/2; infinite e is immediate. The PA function gamma+1/2 attains exactly 1/2. This proves B2 on the continuum, independently of any finite grid.

Furthermore f(z_n)-f(w_n)=1-n^-2 at distance n^-2, so f is not uniformly continuous or globally Lipschitz. At (x,0) with x>0, its inward y-direction quotient is 1-sqrt(x)/sqrt(t), tending to -infinity. A finite convex extension to an open neighborhood would be locally Lipschitz and cannot have this derivative.

A positive weighted orthant is unbalanced along either axis: only one nonzero inward primitive normal contributes. Its boundary star has a proper supporting halfspace, so the positive-spanning mechanism of n2 is unavailable. This proves B3. It is not an original balanced counterexample and receives no mixed-operator application. The complete proof is in argument.md; reports/exact-checks.json contains only finite illustrations of the analytic limiting inequality.

notes.summary: Entire-face matching and common-support compatibility after approximation remain unresolved. Original P05.1/P05.2 classifications remain OPEN.
notes.detailedSummary: The reconstructed theorems give original-function cellwise bounds and independent single-cell majorants, not joint regularization on arbitrary complexes with positive-dimensional overlaps. Finite contacts cannot determine a whole non-PA shared trace. R230's actual unrestricted all-C_b envelopes qualify for the scoped results but still need a genuine compatible global approximation domain before MA. Fixed coefficient categories, actual references and all qualified operator/convergence scopes remain preserved.
notes.text:
The original classification target is retained in both coefficient categories and with the actual admitted reference category: for EVERY admitted bounded PA obstacle, the actual unrestricted envelope must enter the same-reference-growth uniform PC PA closure in that fixed category. Literal PA has integral lattice slopes and rational constants; real PA is its finite real scalar extension retaining rational spatial carriers. A scoped cell theorem, one obstacle, or density in a selected continuous subcone does not complete this target. The associated original contact/operator target requires the actual endpoint to enter a genuine completed global domain before evaluating its contact integral. The full supplied task is preserved unchanged in inputs/retained-task.json.

For an admitted actual positive-growth real PA PC gamma and u∈C_b(X), the literal original envelope uses finite raw printed-PC q with q≤gamma+u and upper-only q≤gamma+O(1). It does not assume competitor continuity. Replacing q by max(q,gamma-||u||∞) preserves printed PCC: the maximum at a center is at most the sum of endpoint maxima. It stays below the obstacle, dominates q and is bounded on both sides relative to gamma. Thus upper-only and two-sided bounded competitor envelopes coincide.
